newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania court gives Dacia Felix licence reprieve.
newsitem.headline: Romania court gives Dacia Felix licence reprieve.

text.p: A Romanian court has overturned a central bank order withdrawing the licence of troubled private bank Dacia Felix SA.

"The court accepted the appeal lodged by Dacia Felix against the National Bank order," judge Ioan Turcu of the Cluj Court of Appeals told reporters on Wednesday. "Consequently, we annulled the BNR order."

The National Bank of Romania (BNR) last month stripped the licence from Dacia Felix, once one of the country's fastest-growing post-communist banks but now struggling with bad debts of some $200 million.
In April Dacia Felix reported a 33.2 billion lei profit for 1996 after a 642.2 billion loss in 1995.
Dacia Felix had challenged removal of its licence saying the BNR had exceeded its powers. It still faces a decision by another Cluj court on a National Bank request for liquidation or reorganisation.

The court ruling in Cluj, where Dacia Felix is based, followed the bank's announcement on Tuesday that a company it identified as American National Group, had agreed to take over its assets and liabilities.
Such a deal would require BNR approval.
No further details have been released on American National in Romania other than that Dacia Felix officials said it managed pension funds in Texas and Delaware. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
